PullRequest.Title: Stale Chat agent accessibility count after workspace-agent deletion

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch to an AI Customizations section and wait for its initial items to load
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The section's provider-backed item fetch and normalization must complete before setSection resolves and the final item-count announcement runs. The diff does not add work before that fetch; sectionLoading suppresses the new autorun announcement during loading, and the existing post-load announcement remains.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: fetchAICustomizationItems obtains customization items from the active item provider; hooks and skills may additionally perform existing file-backed expansion or skill discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One section fetch for a newly observed section. Raw provider enumeration is cached and shared across sections for the active source; section-specific normalization/filtering runs once for the requested section.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider/file discovery and final post-load ARIA announcement occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This fetch remains on the initial section-load critical path. The ARIA update executes only after it settles.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of items returned for the selected section; existing filtering/rendering scales with that count, while the changed announcement formats a count and mutates one of two fixed status nodes in O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A newly observed section starts one fetch. Concurrent section fetches can exist for distinct observed sections, but cachedPromise coalesces raw provider enumeration for the active source. The diff adds no task or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold section observation starts a fetch. Warm active-source provider data is reused through cachedPromise; source changes invalidate it. The diff neither changes cache keys/lifetime nor bypasses coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setSection, sectionLoading, refetchSection, cachedPromise, and aria.status were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and item count vary by harness, but those costs are unchanged. The added fixed DOM update is bounded and occurs after the expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: initial-load boundary count and critical path are unchanged, and duplicate autorun announcements are explicitly suppressed while loading.

Scenarios.Scenario: Delete, add, or update a workspace agent while the Agents section is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The source change invalidates the provider cache, a RunOnceScheduler coalesces same-turn events, and the accepted refresh result updates the observable and rerenders the list. The added ARIA status call then updates a fixed live-region node synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refetch customization items from the active provider after its change event; existing hook/skill sections may perform their existing section-specific file work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one refetch batch per scheduler turn for source events. Each previously observed section is refreshed once; raw provider enumeration is shared by cachedPromise after invalidation. Only the currently bound section's accepted observable update invokes the changed announcement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same coalesced refreshes, filtering, count event, and list rerender occurred, but no ARIA status mutation was made for post-load model updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The refresh boundary must complete before the updated count can be rendered or announced. The diff does not introduce or move the boundary; it adds a constant-size DOM status mutation after completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of same-turn source events after scheduler coalescing, number of previously observed sections for existing refresh work, and current-section item count for existing render work. The new status operation remains one per accepted current-section update and does not scale with item count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-turn source notifications are coalesced by a zero-delay RunOnceScheduler. Observed sections may refetch concurrently, while provider enumeration is promise-coalesced. Sequence checks discard stale results. The changed code starts no asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A source event invalidates cachedPromise once; the following observed-section refreshes share the replacement provider promise. Warm data remains cached until another source change. The announcement has no cache and uses two fixed global status containers, so it retains no growing state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event coalescing, cache invalidation, stale-result checks, observable subscription ownership, and the fixed two-node aria.status implementation were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Change-event frequency depends on provider behavior, but even frequent accepted updates add only one short text replacement and visibility toggle each; there is no geometry read, collection copy, boundary fan-out, or unbounded retention.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds bounded O(1) synchronous DOM work after each coalesced accepted update, with no new expensive boundary, fan-out, or lifecycle growth.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced initial loading, post-load source updates, section subscription replacement, provider/file boundaries, cache behavior, and concurrency. The only runtime change is one fixed-size ARIA live-region update per accepted current-section item update; it is suppressed during initial loading, uses two preallocated nodes, and introduces no actionable performance regression.
